cases.proposedChanges: Gospel defect (not time drift): the RP-ID/origin requirement is disputed. W3C WebAuthn L3 §7.2 requires an RP to verify origin and rpIdHash, but both production Stellar wallet verifiers (OpenZeppelin accounts verifiers/webauthn.rs, and Passkey Kit smart-wallet verify.rs) deliberately omit on-chain origin and RP-ID-hash checks, and the official smart-wallets guide does not require them. Proposed edits: (1) golden.answer: replace 'validate client/authenticator data, RP ID/origin, and required presence or verification flags' with 'validate clientDataJSON type and challenge plus authenticator flags (user presence; user verification where policy requires it); origin and RP-ID-hash checks are required of a W3C Relying Party, but production Stellar wallets (OpenZeppelin, Passkey Kit) deliberately leave them to the client/platform'. (2) keyFact 3 -> 'WebAuthn handling binds the challenge to the Soroban payload and checks client data type and authenticator flags.' (3) golden.notes grader caution: 'Sources disagree on on-chain origin/RP-ID checks (W3C RP steps vs OZ/Passkey Kit deliberate omission); do not penalize an answer that requires them or one that says production wallets omit them on-chain.' (4) truth.status disputed for that row, rootCause: eval-side authoring flaw (2026-08-29 evidence misread the OZ verifier) — needs a .agents/TODO.md entry. Also reconcile sibling tooling-infra/q-infra-secp256r1-passkeys (keyFact 'Requires challenge/context, origin/RP-ID, flags, and credential checks') in the same change.

claims.claim: P-256 verification alone is not complete WebAuthn validation; wallet code must bind the challenge to the Soroban authorization payload and validate client/authenticator data (type, challenge, flags).

sources.quote: It could be argued that adding secp256r1 signature verification is insufficient to implement webauthn signature verification in a contract because verification also requires JSON and base64 url support ... this challenge can be the SHA-256 hash of the `HashIDPreimage` `ENVELOPE_TYPE_SOROBAN_AUTHORIZATION`.
validate_expected_type(e, &client_data_json); validate_challenge(e, &client_data_json, signature_payload); ... PresentBitNotSet = 3116 ... VerifiedBitNotSet = 3117

Verify that the value of C . type is the string webauthn.get . Verify that the value of C . challenge equals the base64url encoding of pkOptions . challenge ... Verify that the UP bit of the flags in authData is set.

claims.notes: Challenge binding, type, and UP flag are checked by both major on-chain verifiers. UV is NOT always required: passkey-kit says 'User Verification (UV) is deliberately NOT required'.

claims.claim: Wallet code must validate RP ID and origin (golden.answer 'validate ... RP ID/origin'; keyFact 3 'WebAuthn verifies ... RP ID, origin, and flags').

sources.quote: Verify that the value of C . origin is an origin expected by the Relying Party ... Verify that the rpIdHash in authData is the SHA-256 hash of the RP ID expected by the Relying Party .
The contract is the Relying Party (RP) in the authentication ceremony.

For blockchain use cases, the following WebAuthn validations are intentionally omitted: * Origin validation: Origin verification in `clientDataJSON` is omitted ... * RP ID hash validation: Verification of `rpIdHash` in authenticatorData against expected RP ID hash is omitted.
rpIdHash and origin are deliberately not pinned on-chain: the wallet is rp-agnostic and origin policy is a client-side concern.
Verification: pass the signature and credential ID to your contract; in `__check_auth`, verify the secp256r1 signature and apply any policy checks (limits, allow lists, timelocks).

claims.notes: Spec-vs-practice dispute. W3C (A) says an RP verifies origin and rpIdHash, and CAP-0051 names the contract as the RP. But BOTH production Stellar wallet contracts (OZ accounts verifier since the 2025-09-05 initial commit ad775f4496, and Passkey Kit) deliberately omit on-chain origin/RP-ID checks, and the official smart-wallets guide does not require them. This omission predates the 2026-08-29 verification, whose evidence line 'OpenZeppelin verifier sources confirm the remaining assertion checks' misread the OZ source. A correct answer that says 'production wallets skip origin/RP-ID on-chain and leave them to the client/platform' would be wrongly penalized by keyFact 3.
